title: What If We Planted a Trillion Trees?

scenes.text: What if we planted a trillion trees? One study says there's room, and the carbon numbers are huge.
Researchers mapped where forests could grow without touching farms or cities. They found about nine hundred million hectares, roughly the size of the United States.
Once grown, those trees could hold about two hundred and five gigatonnes of carbon, roughly two thirds of what humans have emitted.
That could cut the carbon in the atmosphere by around a quarter.
But not tomorrow. New forests take decades to mature, and warming could shrink the room by about a fifth by 2050.
The map shows where trees could grow. It doesn't plant a single one.

What if we planted a trillion trees?
A 2019 study in Science found room for about 900 million hectares of new forest, which could hold around 205 gigatonnes of carbon, though it would take decades.
